Real load order settles us before the provider has a session context, so its reply states no session while the announcement that follows states it — so an answer naming no session is now read as the provider making no identity claim (not a protocol failure, not success evidence), while a refusal/unreadable version stay protocol failures, a statement naming another session is an identity failure, and a refused registration is a registration failure whether or not anything answers (the WIP reported it as none). ask() keeps the session-less reply as last resort and waits for a stating statement within the same budget, and unsubscribes both channels.
